# Margin

A small Next.js bookshelf for tracking books you are reading and books you have finished. Add a title, author, and optional notes; open a book to see its details and copy a direct link to its page.

## Run it

Requires Node.js 20.9 or newer.

1. Run \`npm install\`
2. Run \`npm run dev\`
3. Open [http://localhost:3000](http://localhost:3000)

For a production run, use \`npm run build\` followed by \`npm run start\`.

## Where books are saved

Books are stored in \`data/books.json\`. The app creates the file if it is missing and writes changes atomically. The file stays in place when the server restarts.

You can set \`BOOKS_FILE\` to an absolute path if you want the JSON file elsewhere. Run the app on a server with a writable, persistent filesystem; ephemeral serverless filesystems will not retain changes.

item.text:
Built the Next.js bookshelf app. The home page shows books you’re reading and books you’ve finished. You can add a title, author, and notes; mark a book finished; and open a shareable page for each book with a copy-link button.

Books are saved in [data/books.json](/workspace/data/books.json), with no database or accounts. Run it with `npm install` and `npm run dev`; [README.md](/workspace/README.md) has the production instructions. The server needs a writable, persistent filesystem for books to survive restarts.

I verified the production build and type check, then added a book, opened its direct link, marked it finished, and confirmed it was still there after restarting the server.
